rooms.title: Idempotency Gone Wrong
rooms.description: You have an Ansible task that keeps reporting 'changed' on every run. Figure out why and propose a fix that restores idempotency.

artifacts.label: roles/web/tasks/main.yml
artifacts.content:
---
- name: Deploy web config
  copy:
    src: files/web.conf
    dest: /etc/web.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0644'
    force: yes

params.prompt_label: Propose a fix (describe the change you would make to this task):

hints.text: Look closely at the copy module options. Which one might force a change every run?
If the destination file already exists and contents match, the task should be 'ok' not 'changed'.
Remove or change 'force: yes'. For example set 'force: no' so the copy only updates when contents differ.

on_failure.message: You exhausted your attempts on this idempotency puzzle.

rooms.title: Configuration Stable
rooms.description: Nice work. The playbook is now idempotent and only reports changes when something actually changed.

hints.text: Idempotency means running the play multiple times leads to the same end state.
Options like 'force: yes' can break idempotency if misused.
Use 'force' only when you truly want to overwrite a file unconditionally.

rooms.title: Config Chaos
rooms.description: You weren’t able to restore idempotency this time. Review what went wrong and try again later.

hints.text: The copy module is idempotent by default when contents don't change.
Forcing a copy each run removes idempotency.
Focus your fix on the 'force' option in the task.
